Contributing to readboj

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

readboj is an R client for official Bank of Japan (BOJ) statistical services. Version 0.2.0 is a pre-CRAN release. Contributions should preserve the package’s auditable request identity, bounded resource use, deterministic offline path, and documented return contracts.

Before reporting a problem or opening a pull request

Please email chartwellmacro@gmail.com before substantial changes. For a parser or normalisation problem, start with a packaged synthetic fixture so that the report does not depend on a changing BOJ response:

path <- system.file("extdata", "api-data-page-1.json", package = "readboj")
local_data <- read_boj_snapshot(path, type = "data_json", db = "FM08")
local_data[c("series_code", "period", "value", "value_status")]

The fixtures in inst/extdata/ are deliberately synthetic; they are not official BOJ observations. A live check is available only when it is useful for a service-availability or current-schema report:

READBOJ_LIVE_TESTS=true Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()'

Live requests depend on the current BOJ service and its current data. Do not make the default test suite, examples, or a pull request depend on network availability. Use a temporary cache_dir while developing and use offline = TRUE or read_boj_snapshot() when a deterministic replay is possible.

Pull requests

Keep changes focused and explain the user-visible reason for them. In particular:

  • preserve exported signatures, defaults, output column order and types, readboj_provenance, typed error classes, cache bounds, and HTTPS/host restrictions unless a deliberately reviewed compatibility change is being proposed;
  • add or update deterministic tests for changed parsing, identity, error, or resource-boundary behavior;
  • keep examples and vignettes runnable without credentials or a live network;
  • update roxygen source, generated reference pages, README/articles, and NEWS together when documentation or a public contract changes; and
  • retain inst/NOTICE/bojapi-MIT.txt, official BOJ service credit, and any provenance or permission information when adapting third-party material.

Before submitting, run the focused tests you changed and the full local test suite:

Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()'

If documentation or package metadata is changed, also run the relevant documentation build and R CMD check locally. Report the exact commands and results; do not describe a live, platform-specific, or unavailable check as passing.

What to include in a report

Include the smallest reproducible example, the readboj version, R version, operating system, and relevant sessionInfo(). For a returned object, include the names, classes, dimensions, and a redacted summary from boj_provenance(x). For an error, include its condition class, message, warnings, and (when present) the canonical URL/query, HTTP status, response format/encoding, and raw SHA-256. Redact local paths, tokens, credentials, personal data, and any unrelated private request content. Use the security process for a suspected vulnerability rather than publishing exploit details in an issue or pull request.

License and provenance

Package code: MIT, copyright Chartwell Macro. That package licence does not reassign rights in Bank of Japan data, publications, services, or other upstream material. The package includes a preserved third-party MIT notice and uses official BOJ services subject to their own credit and use terms. If a contribution adapts external code, data, or text, record its source and permission in the pull request and preserve the relevant notice. Do not add real BOJ response payloads to fixtures; use small synthetic fixtures or a documented, opt-in live canary.
